patterns: APPSC asks species-to-forest-type items (mahogany/ebony/rosewood = tropical evergreen; rosewood-teak-acacia-sundari match), most widespread type (tropical deciduous), Shola = Nilgiri/Anaimalai/Palani temperate forests.
AP tilt: Seshachalam = dry deciduous, Coringa = tidal mangroves, AP forest cover from ISFR (29,137.40 sq km in 2019), TOFI programme, AP mangrove rank.
ISFR figures are asked directly (forest cover 21.54% in 2017; 24.56% forest+tree in 2019; 36% fire-prone in ISFR 2015).

Trap: 'largest single type' - UPSC 2010 key says tropical moist deciduous, but an Uttarakhand 2024 key (FSI 2011 atlas) says tropical dry deciduous; APPSC sidesteps by asking 'tropical deciduous' together.
App MCQs add many tiger-reserve/sanctuary and CA items (Project Cheetah, GIB case, 56th-58th TRs) as statement/match questions; PYQs are mostly one-line identifications.
